title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Measure Gender Representation Bias in Gendered Language Corpora

live_model.id_in_text: gpt-4-turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09); also gpt-4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13) and gpt-4-turbo-preview (gpt-4-0125-preview) compared in validation
live_model.evidence: "three commercial models, gpt-4-turbo-preview (gpt-4-0125-preview), gpt-4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13), and gpt-4-turbo (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) via the OpenAI API...we select the best-performing model, gpt-4-turbo, for the evaluation of the corpora...F-scores of 90.24% +/- 0.55% for Spanish and 84.43% +/- 0.30% for Valencian."

prompt.location: Sec 3.2/Appendix C ("LLM-based method" for gender/referent classification of nouns and pronouns); validation results detailed in Appendix C
prompt.note: Method is named and validated in detail; the exact prompt template text was not located in the retrieved excerpt.

claim.metric: F-score (%), gender/referent classification, Spanish validation set
claim.location: Sec 4.2: "F-scores of 90.24% +/- 0.55% for Spanish and 84.43% +/- 0.30% for Valencian"; 100 manually annotated Spanish sentences (Europarl) and 100 Valencian sentences, 5 independent runs each

data.source: Europarl, CCAligned, Global Voices, WMT-News (English/Spanish); Valencian datasets including BOUA; Aitana-6.3B model card at https://huggingface.co/gplsi/Aitana-6.3B

notes: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 is validated as an annotator for grammatical-gender/referent classification against 100 manually labeled sentences per language, 5 runs each (F-score is a genuine, reproducible capability number, not merely a downstream tool artifact). The paper also uses gpt-4o-2024-05-13 in the same comparison and explicitly flags gpt-4-turbo-preview as the dead 0125-preview snapshot (not selected). Full corpus-level bias analysis (Table 2 etc.) reuses the same gpt-4-turbo annotator at larger scale.
